svg.aria-label: Boot chains of 5 boards aligned by job: i.MX 8M Plus: Boot ROM, then U-Boot SPL, then TF-A BL31, then OP-TEE (BL32), then U-Boot (BL33), then Linux 6.18; STM32MP1: Boot ROM, then TF-A BL2, then OP-TEE, then U-Boot, then Linux 6.18; STM32MP2: Boot ROM, then TF-A BL2, then TF-A BL31, then OP-TEE (BL32), then U-Boot (BL33), then Linux 6.18; Zynq-7000: BootROM, then U-Boot SPL (BOOT.BIN), then U-Boot (u-boot.img), then Linux 6.18; Jetson Orin Nano: BootROM + PSC ROM, then MB1, then MB2, then TF-A + OP-TEE, then UEFI + L4TLauncher, then Linux 5.15 (tegra). The columns are the five jobs every chain has to do: Boot ROM, first loader, secure world, bootloader and kernel.
svg.text: The same five jobs in the same order. The names, the privilege levels and the place each one is stored change.
secure world on the CPU complex
Dashed outline: optional, not part of the default build. Privilege levels: EL3 secure monitor, S-EL1 trusted OS, EL2 or EL1 non-secure.
The interactive version of this chart, with every stage's job, storage and build command, is on the page that shows it.
